"You've maintained your innocence from the beginning. I believe you."

 A young man in a guard's uniform steps up to the bars and begins fumbling with a keyring.

 "My name is Greave. I thought I was coming here to keep people safe, but the other guards are thugs. They don't care who deserves to be here and who doesn't. I'm getting out of here, but there's no way I'm leaving an innocent person in this pit."

 The door clicks open, and Greave looks straight at you.

 "This might be a bit rough. You got any experience with a weapon or anything?"

Peering into the bars through a wild shock of hair is the wry face of a young orc. He begins to work the lock open quietly.

"Name's Kirilo. I escaped a while back, but I saw the boat come in, and... well I remember sitting in one of these cells myself, just wishing someone would come and help."

The lock quietly snaps open and the door goes slack. Kirilo, barefoot and dressed in scant more than tatters and a ragged cloak, pushes it open and motions you out into the hall.

"Now the fun starts. You got any tricks up your sleeve I should know about?"

"Well at least you're smart enough not to shit me."

A man the size of an ox steps up to the bars and begins to struggle with the lock.

"Some of the guards thought it'd be fun to take me out of the cell for a little sport, but now they're fuckin' dead, and I got their boots. And the key to your cell, 'parently."

The lock clicks open, and he wastes no time throwing the door wide. He's been stripped, but has a hastily-gathered pack of things, presumably scavenged from the guards he killed.

"Call me Leftie. And tell me you can fight, cuz I ain't fucking carrying you."

A mountainous orc with a bald head and a neatly-trimmed beard steps up to the bars and begins quietly undoing the lock.

"I am called Nazar, friend. I broke into this place looking for someone, but all I found was this key, and I don't like leaving empty-handed. Lucky for you!"

The door clicks open, and Nazar stands before you, olive-skinned, barrel-chested, and fur-clad.

"You can thank me later. For now, we have to get out of here, and I can't promise it'll be easy. Can you fight if we need to?"

An athletic man with a bandana tied over his forehead steps up to the bars and begins silently working the lock open. He has a broad grin, but his eyebrows are covered so his expression is difficult to read.

"I broke in to raid their supplies, but they ain't got shit right now. Saw this key on the desk though, and thought a prison break sounded like fun. You agree, of course."

Quiet as a whisper, the door swings open. The man is clearly an accomplished burglar, and seems dressed for the occasion.

"I'm Peregrine, by the way. Ready to roll?"

en:
"Wait, an actual necromancer? I didn't think-"

The man's voice is cut off in a strangled cry, as he is slammed against the bars by a gigantic, nearly naked man the size of an ox. In the space of just a few moments, the large man breaks the smaller one's neck, then searches his body. Finding nothing to his liking, he takes the dead man's boots and leaves.

You stand and peer through the bars and see the key, presumably to your cell, on the floor just a few feet away.

The opportunity could not be better. With a simple incantation, you sieze on the moment of the guard's death to push his corpse into unlife and bind it to your will, unlocking the door and releasing you.

You gather yourself and set forth.

A sprightly young woman with a full head of auburn curls steps up to the bars and begins to work the lock.

"You know, I've broken out of a few prisons in my time, but I've got a good feeling about this one. The guards are all morons, as far as I can tell. Also, hi. I'm Rosaline. Come with?"

She pushes the door open as the lock clicks, and motions you out into the hallway. She has the look of a dancer, but it's clear that right now, she isn't fooling around.

"Well, ready to go? Oh wait, please don't tell me that I rescued a baker or something. You can fight or at least hide or something, yeah?"

A man with grizzled hair and a dour expression steps up to the bars and begins to unlock the door.

"I'm Shapiro, a sorcerer. I managed to snag a few keys from the guard as he passed by my cell, but there's no telling how long it'll be before they discover something is amiss."

The door swings open gently as the lock is undone. Shapiro is dressed in what must have once have been a grand magister's robe, now soiled and tattered, and he looks very tired.

"We don't have much time, and we'll need some kind of strategy. I can cast some simple spells. What should I expect of you?"

A very tall orc with a long and well-kept beard steps up to the bars and gets to work unlocking your cell.

"I am Vankan, stranger. I've been here quite some time, but I took advantage of the commotion of the new arrivals to steal some keys. I got the one for my cell, and apparently the one for yours."

The lock clicks and the door swings open, and you can see that Vankan has made an attempt to make himself presentable, despite being clothed in tattered furs.

"And now, we're both free. Comparitively, anyway. We've still got to get out of the compound. I can cast a few spells if you... what do you do, exactly?"

"You, then, are the one I have been seeking!"

A clawed hand reaches into the bars and peels the door from its hinges. On the other side stands a creature that can only be a demon from the pit of hell. He is the size of lean man, but his skin has the color and sheen of an open wound, and his grinning face is crowned with sharp horns.

"Your call has been answered, and I, Zantanak, have come to serve."

He bows and presents the hallway to you as any gracious host might, before standing straight and brandishing a horribly jagged spear.

"There yet remain fools blocking the way. Are you well enough to fight?"

en:
Over the next few days, you are taken by boat to the island of Lukatt. 

An angry wind whips heavy rain as you are put on a lifeboat with another man in chains and jettisoned some distance from the shore. 

The current carries you rapidly toward a short cove where men in guards' uniforms wait to receive you. Without a word, you are dragged from the boat and up the path to the old fortress that houses the Stocks, and thrown, soaked and shivering, into your cell where you will wait for the execution of your sentence.
